blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from City of Maple Ridge, Maple Ridge Museum, TransLink, School District 42 and BC government pages, and it replaces text repeated on the other Maple Ridge guides.
Uptown Haney: how the east side of the Town Centre took shape

The Maple Ridge Museum says that before the Lougheed Highway was finished, central Haney was mostly farmland. The exceptions were the sides of 8th Avenue (now 224 Street), the old Aggie grounds and hall on land that had belonged to Thomas Haney, and three schools. When the highway gave Maple Ridge its first proper cross-town road, businesses moved uphill from the river landing, and the post office followed in 1936.

Schools mark the east side's early growth. The museum records that the first school in the Haney townsite centre opened on December 28, 1908, on Hinch Road (now 225 Street) roughly where the Leisure Centre stands today. It had two rooms and 59 pupils in its first year. A larger Haney Central School replaced it in 1923 on the same property, about where the western half of Haney Place Mall now sits. An 1888 school stood at Dewdney Trunk Road and Lillooet Road, today's 232 Street.

blocks.text: Sport, skating and the arts

The City lists the Telosky Stadium field upgrades as complete. On April 16, 2026 it unveiled two accessible bleachers and a Legacy Grove of shade trees there, projects from the 2024 BC Summer Games. The stadium, skate plaza and Thomas Haney Secondary share one site.

The ACT Arts Centre is now City-run: the City says it took over operating the centre on January 1, 2026, from the Maple Ridge Pitt Meadows Arts Council. The City's facility page lists a 486-seat main stage and a flat-floor studio theatre of about 2,311 sq ft.
Getting around: Maple Meadows Station
Maple Meadows Station, at 20010 Dunn Avenue, is the West Coast Express stop in the northwest corner of Hammond, at the west end of the city and a long way from 230 Street.

TransLink's park-and-ride page lists 435 spaces there, open from 4 a.m. to 2 a.m. at $3 a day or $60 a month, with no overnight parking. The bike parkade is listed as open at $1 a day (up to $8 a month) and needs a registered Compass Card. Lockers rent for $10 a month plus GST with a three-month minimum.

The West Coast Express timetable effective September 7, 2026 shows five weekday departures from Maple Meadows to Waterfront, at 5:50, 6:20, 6:50, 7:20 and 7:50 a.m., taking about 50 minutes. Evening trains arrive back at 4:38, 5:08, 5:38, 6:18 and 7:08 p.m. There is no weekend or holiday service.
What the plans mean if you own or buy here

The City's Town Centre Area Plan is the one that matters for lots in the Town Centre, and the City adopted its latest update on November 25, 2025. The Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan is a different document. The City describes it as running along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road from the western boundary to 221 Street, and the four proposed bus rapid transit stations it lists are at 203 Street, 207 Street, Laity Street and 216 Street. All four are west of the Town Centre, so by the City's description east-side lots fall outside it.

The City also states that the corridor plan does not change zoning or approve construction. The City says development applications are now accepted there, with a pre-application meeting generally required. A plan designation tells you what the City expects over many years, not what you can build next month, so ask the City about the zone on any lot you are considering.

Out west, the Hammond Area Plan says residential and mixed-use buildings near Maple Meadows Station generally run 8 to 12 storeys depending on distance from the station, and the plan says the station was designated a Transit-Oriented Area in 2024. The City dates the Port Hammond Junction Township to 1883, and the Maple Ridge Museum says Interfor announced the Hammond Cedar Mill closure in fall 2019.
Flood history and what to check

The Maple Ridge Museum holds a June 1948 aerial photo of central Haney looking south toward the Fraser at the height of that year's flood. The City publishes Fraser River and Alouette River floodplain maps, shows the area expected to flood on average once every 200 years, and says it manages flood risk case by case. I found no flood statement written for the east side as a whole, so look up the exact address.
Maple Ridge home prices, September 2026

The MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for a typical Maple Ridge home was $882,600 in September 2026, down 7.0% from a year earlier. Detached homes were $1,155,900 (down 7.7% over the year), townhouses $700,800 (down 8.1%) and apartments $513,400 (down 2.6%).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 72 in June to 75 in October (+4.2%), and it took 19.8% of the city’s 247 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 112 in June to 106 in October (−5.4%), and it took 40.4% of the city’s 230 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out East Central for detached houses in July (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in June, September (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in August, October (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June (a buyers’ best bet).

faq.q: Where does East Central Maple Ridge begin and end?
faq.a: East Central is an MLS sub-area name and the City does not publish its boundary. The City's Town Centre Area Plan is the nearest official guide.

faq.q: Which high school is on the east side of the Town Centre?
faq.a: Thomas Haney Secondary, at 23000 116 Avenue. The school says it opened in September 1992 and runs a self-directed learning model. Its grade range differs by source: the BC government listing says Grades 7 to 12 and the school's own page says Grade 8 to 12. Confirm catchments with SD42 by address.

The City lists two synthetic softball diamonds, overlapping synthetic soccer fields, LED lighting on all four diamonds, a new washroom and fieldhouse, and the Thomas Haney Youth Action Park skate plaza of about 17,000 sq ft, at 23000 116 Avenue.

faq.q: Is there a youth centre nearby?
faq.a: Yes. The Greg Moore Youth Centre is at 11925 Haney Place. The City says it has operated for over 25 years and lists climbing and bouldering walls, an indoor skate park and a multi-sport court. Check the City's page for current hours.

faq.q: How much is parking at Maple Meadows Station?
faq.a: TransLink lists 435 spaces at $3 a day or $60 a month, open 4 a.m. to 2 a.m., with no overnight parking. Check TransLink's page for current rates.

faq.q: Does the Lougheed corridor plan cover the east side?
faq.a: Not according to the City's description. The corridor plan runs from the western boundary to 221 Street, and its four proposed bus rapid transit stops are at 203 Street, 207 Street, Laity Street and 216 Street. The City also says the plan does not change zoning or approve construction.

faq.q: Who runs The ACT Arts Centre now?
faq.a: The City of Maple Ridge, since January 1, 2026. It was previously run by the Maple Ridge Pitt Meadows Arts Council.

The Maple Ridge Museum has an aerial photo of central Haney during the June 1948 Fraser River flood. Today the City publishes floodplain maps and asks owners near the floodplain to check the exact address, since rules differ lot by lot.
